newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says repulses attack on Eritrea border.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says repulses attack on Eritrea border.

text.p: The Sudanese army said on Wednesday it had repulsed an attack by opposition forces and Eritreans on the border with Eritrea.
In a statement carried by the official Sudan news agency, SUNA, army spokesman Lieutenant General Mohammed al-Senouse Ahmed said the opposition attacked the area of Atokar at dawn.
He said the attackers, including Eritreans, were destroyed and "pockets of them were chased up to the Eritrean border".
The attackers fled leaving arms and ammunition which the army seized, Ahmed said.
Eritrea supports opposition groups fighting to oust Khartoum's Islamist-backed government which it says is destablising the region.
There have been several reports over the past few months of cross-border attacks staged by Sudanese opposition based in Eritrea.

Sudan said on Monday it would soon put on trial a number of people who took part in an alleged plot to attack government targets in Port Sudan with Eritrean help and overthrow President Omar Hassan al-Bashir.
Defence Minister Lieutenant General Hasan Abdel-Rahman Ali told parliament that Eritrean troops were set to help opposition party members with the takeover of the port.
